title: Flagship validation
hypothesis: The base Trend+Carry book survives Monte Carlo, sensitivity and crisis tests.
question: Is the deployed base book robust: to resampling, to parameter changes, to crises, and to expanding the universe?
prior: A validated book should sit on a plateau, not a peak.
citations: Bailey, D. & López de Prado, M. (2014). The Deflated Sharpe Ratio. JPM 40(5).
method: 5,000-path block bootstrap (21-day blocks); 12 single-parameter perturbations; 7 crisis windows; a 51-ETF universe expansion.
verdict_reason: Sharpe 1.03, MaxDD −10.6%, correlation to SPY −0.04. Bootstrap 5th-percentile Sharpe +0.67 with no path below zero; every perturbation stayed within 0.93–1.12. Expanding the universe lowered Sharpe to 0.93, so we kept the base universe.
lessons: More names meant more cost and complexity for no edge.
curves_note: Curves regenerated on the 2026-09-11 cache with the v39 code (legacy signal); the table is the June 2026 run.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
